title: IdeNtification of shared and divergent pathoMechanisms IN AcuTe and chrOnic uRticaria (NOMINATOR)
summary: This study aims to better understand what causes the disease and how it develops in the skin and blood of participants. Researchers will collect and examine blood, skin samples, and fluid from body tissues to look for new clues and possible links. The study is exploratory, meaning it aims to identify patterns and connections rather than test or prove a specific idea.

1. Visit (Day 1):
The patient is given a detailed explanation of the study, potential risks, and the procedure. The patient must provide informed consent in order to participate. Inclusion and exclusion criteria are reviewed.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•    The patient is capable of giving informed consent.
•    The patient can communicate with the principal investigator, understands the study requirements, and is willing to follow them.
•    The patient is of legal age (18 years or older)
•    The patient has
- acute urticaria (<2 weeks) or
- chronic spontaneous urticaria, defined by the following criteria:
a. according to international guidelines
b. the definitions listed above:

- active CSU, ≤12 months (CSUsho, including up to n=5 patients receiving omalizumab therapy)
- active CSU, ≥3 years (CSUlo, of which up to n=5 patients received omalizumab therapy)
- previous, now resolved CSU (pastCSU, defined as patients who showed no CSU symptoms for ≥6 months and did not receive CSU-specific medication
Exclusion criteria:
•    Patients with a history of or current treatment with ciclosporin, dupilumab, anti-KIT antibodies, and/or BTK inhibitors
•    Patients with a history of or current long-term therapy (≥ 1 week with ≥ 7.5 mg oral prednisolone equivalent) with corticosteroids
•    Patients with an interval of ≥ 24 hours after administration of a systemic corticosteroid
•    Patients with other conditions associated with urticaria/angioedema symptoms (urticarial vasculitis, erythema multiforme, mastocytosis, hereditary or acquired angioedema, e.g., due to C1 inhibitor deficiency).
•	Active skin diseases (e.g., atopic dermatitis, bullous pemphigoid, dermatitis herpetiformis, etc.).
•    Pregnant or breastfeeding women.
